mfg1-mechanical-lesson-071.title: Connect prohibition and warning signs to actions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-071.objective: Connect prohibition and warning signs to actions, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Prohibition signs identify actions that must not be taken. No smoking and no open flames have different targets: a no-flames area requires attention to ignition sources other than smoking as well. Read the particular action covered by signs such as do not touch, not drinking water, no running or rushing in, and prohibitions on phones or electronic equipment. A sign is not permission to approach and test the hazard.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Warning signs indicate that a hazard exists. Obstacles, upward steps, downward steps, slippery floors, falls, overhead hazards and electric shock are different hazards. Do not identify the hazard from a general warning triangle alone; read the text and check its location. An upward and downward step require different foot movements, so do not assume their pictures mean the same thing.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Tsunami danger areas, landslides and falling-rock signs relate to evacuation or passage decisions, separately from equipment-operation warnings. If a sign is dirty or hidden by goods, report its location and condition. In study, match sign names to necessary actions without independently changing workplace access controls.

terms.meaning: A sign identifying an action that is prohibited.
A sign indicating a dangerous or harmful condition.
A sign calling attention to overhead objects or restricted headroom.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-072.title: Distinguish chemical labels from emergency-location signs
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-072.objective: Distinguish chemical labels from emergency-location signs, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: The source’s chemical pictograms include a flame for flammability and related hazards; liquid attacking a hand or metal for corrosion; a person with a chest symbol for health hazards; a fish and tree for aquatic environmental hazards; and an exclamation mark for acute toxicity, skin or eye irritation and similar hazards. Pictures help distinguish hazards; they do not identify a substance or a safe concentration by themselves. Read the label and SDS together.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: An AED sign identifies the location of an automated external defibrillator. An AED is a medical device supporting electrical treatment of abnormal heart rhythms. Having seen the sign does not mean you have received training. In an emergency, follow reporting procedures, voice guidance and workplace training. Check extinguisher locations together with escape routes in normal conditions too.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: An extensive-area evacuation space, a building used for evacuation and a tsunami evacuation site do not necessarily serve the same purpose. Do not confuse evacuation to a broad outdoor space with tsunami evacuation to a tall building or similar place. Confirm routes suitable for the disaster type through the introduction and evacuation plan before work, rather than searching for signs in an emergency.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-073.title: Connect OSHMS and quality PDCA through records
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-073.objective: Connect OSHMS and quality PDCA through records, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: OSHMS is a company system for managing occupational safety and health. Planning organizes hazards and goals; implementation carries out measures and training; evaluation checks activities and results; improvement reviews causes and the next plan. Writing a countermeasure once does not complete ongoing management.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Quality-management PDCA also cycles through planning, doing, checking or evaluating, and improving. A plan links goals to concrete actions; implementation follows the plan; checking compares results with goals; improvement feeds the next plan. Safety-measure records and product-quality records have different targets, so organize their relationship without mixing them together.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: In the three-realities approach, the workplace is where the problem occurs, the actual item is the object concerned, and actual facts are what is verified there. Do not conclude from meeting-room guesses alone; compare records with what can be observed safely. One improved number after action does not rule out other times or remaining hazards. Set the next check date and responsible person.

paragraphs.title: Apply the cycle to environmental goals
paragraphs.text: A circular economy considers reducing waste and pollution from design, circulating products and materials through repair, reuse and resource recovery, and regenerating nature through renewable energy and ecosystem restoration. In factory improvement plans, separate goals for generation, energy and other factors from recovery quantities, and connect action with results checks. Environmental targets do not authorize omitting safety-related protection or packaging on your own.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-074.title: Distinguish variable data, attribute data and actions after sampling
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-074.objective: Distinguish variable data, attribute data and actions after sampling, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Data measured as continuous quantities, such as length or mass, are variable data; counts such as scratches or nonconforming units are attribute data. A measured shaft diameter and the number of shafts whose diameters are out of specification are different information. Match units and record fields; do not put a measurement directly into a count field.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: A lot is a group of products made under the same conditions or otherwise managed together. Sampling inspection selects specimens by the specified method and judges using sample size, acceptance number and related conditions. Do not select only convenient good units, or treat sample results as individual guarantees for every uninspected unit.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Possible actions for a rejected lot include returning purchased goods, sorting by inspecting all items and separating conforming units, or rework. The choice follows the quality staff’s judgment and procedures. Workers must not remove nonconforming labels and ship; keep the target and its judgment identifiable.

terms.meaning: Data measured as continuous quantities, such as length.
Data counted as numbers of units or occurrences.
An action separating items according to specified conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-075.title: Distinguish tensile properties and five hardness tests
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-075.objective: Distinguish tensile properties and five hardness tests, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Tensile strength is the maximum stress in a tensile test. Yield strength is a reference stress associated with the onset of progressive plastic deformation. Elongation after fracture relates to the increase in gauge length after fracture. Young’s modulus expresses the stress–strain relationship in the elastic range. Do not call the elongation at one moment under load the elongation after fracture or tensile strength.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Rockwell hardness uses indentation depth, with a scale following HR. Brinell uses the diameter of a ball indentation, written HBW in the tungsten-carbide-ball example. Vickers hardness HV uses the diagonals of a square-pyramidal indentation; Knoop hardness HK uses the long diagonal of an elongated diamond-shaped indentation. The source gives thin layers as an example where Knoop may be considered.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Shore hardness uses the rebound height of a dropped hammer. Separate the measured quantities: depth, diameter, diagonals and rebound height. Equal numbers on different scales are not directly comparable. Check the indentation’s effect, the uses of specimens and products, load and other conditions under the specified method.

terms.meaning: A reference stress associated with the onset of progressive plastic deformation.
Hardness using the long diagonal of an elongated indentation.
Hardness using rebound height and related conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-076.title: Distinguish the targets of eddy-current and sensory inspection
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-076.objective: Distinguish the targets of eddy-current and sensory inspection, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Eddy-current testing, ET, brings a coil carrying alternating current near the object and examines electrical changes in the coil associated with eddy currents in the object. Conductivity, shape and other conditions affect applicability, so this is not a method used identically on every material. Penetrant testing of surface-opening defects and magnetic-particle testing near the surface of magnetizable objects use different principles.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Senses include sight, hearing, smell, touch and taste. The source gives examples of checking scratches or color by sight, sound by hearing and roughness by touch. This does not authorize tasting unknown factory liquids or bringing a nose or hand near chemicals. Perform specified sensory evaluation only on permitted targets under safe conditions.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: When using human senses, match reference samples, lighting, distance and judging conditions. Assessing quality that is difficult to quantify is different from changing acceptance based on personal preference. The later source also describes magnetic-flux-leakage inspection. Do not combine magnetic-particle, eddy-current and flux-leakage methods into one procedure under one name; confirm the specified method with the responsible person.

terms.meaning: Circulating currents induced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field.
Inspection using human senses.
The phenomenon of magnetic flux leaking outside a material.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-077.title: Select measuring aids according to their roles
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-077.objective: Select measuring aids according to their roles, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: A straightedge has a highly straight reference face and is used for marking or guidance. A square helps check the right-angle relationship between faces. Inside and outside calipers help transfer dimensions such as difficult-to-access internal or external diameters. Calipers of this transfer type alone are not the same as a measuring instrument displaying a number.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: A surface gauge has a pointed tip and a holding structure, helping mark parallel lines or check heights. A V-block supports cylindrical and similar objects in a V-shaped groove. A box angle block uses grooves and related features to secure objects; a magnetic base fixes a measuring instrument using a magnet and holding structure. Similar names do not make holding and measurement the same function.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: When selecting an aid, diagram the target shape, reference face, direction of movement and fixing position. Placing a cylinder on a V-block does not mean every dimension has been measured. Check dirt, tilt and loose fixing, and use the specified method to avoid including deformation from excessive clamping in the result.

terms.meaning: An aid for checking a right-angle relationship.
An instrument with a pointed part supporting marking and related work.
An aid used to hold or fix a target.
